_comment: The decision table. Columns are fixed by the UI; rows editable by the nightly maintenance job.

rows.when: The task fits in one session. Always the first resort - memory infrastructure you don't build can't rot.
rows.retrieval: None needed - everything is already in attention.
rows.cant: Persist past the session; scale past the window; stay cheap as history grows.
rows.watch: Context rot: quality degrades well before the hard token limit.

rows.when: Single user or project, human oversight matters, corpus under a few thousand entries. The right default for coding agents and personal assistants.
rows.cant: Match paraphrase (“can't eat peanuts” ≠ “allergy”); enforce structure; serve many users.
rows.watch: Silent bloat and contradiction - nothing forces maintenance.

rows.when: Session state and scratch data that should expire on its own; latency budgets in single-digit milliseconds.
rows.retrieval: Exact key lookup; TTL does the forgetting for free.
rows.cant: Search by content at all - you must know the key.
rows.watch: TTL is a blunt instrument: it forgets by age, not by value.

rows.when: Memories have structure worth enforcing - types, subjects, timestamps, supersession chains - and you want deterministic, debuggable retrieval.
rows.retrieval: Exact filters, recency ordering, BM25 keyword via FTS.
rows.cant: Semantic similarity (without a vector extension); flexible schema evolution.
rows.watch: Schema decisions are write policies - migrate carefully.

rows.when: Large heterogeneous history, many users, or queries that won't share words with what was stored. The recall layer of most memory products.
rows.retrieval: k-NN semantic similarity; hybrid BM25 + rerank in production.
rows.cant: Read its own contents - no native update, contradiction, or time handling.
rows.watch: Similar ≠ relevant; “allergic to peanuts” sits near “loves peanut butter”.

rows.when: Relationships and time carry the value: multi-hop questions, facts with lifespans, fusing conversational and business data.
rows.retrieval: Entry-node search + bounded traversal; time-scoped queries (“as of June”).
rows.cant: Stay cheap - every write is several LLM calls of extraction and resolution.
rows.watch: Entity-resolution mistakes compound structurally and are painful to undo.

rows.when: Production systems at scale. Typical stack: KV for session state, vectors for recall, relational or graph as the source of truth.
rows.retrieval: Several strategies in parallel, fused and reranked.
rows.cant: Stay simple - you now maintain every layer you added.
rows.watch: Consistency between layers becomes its own maintenance job.
